basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 62.' and it opens '(Vers. 62 et 63.) Et ipse habitabat in terra Austri: et egressus est Isaac exerceri in'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 62 et 63.) Et ipse habitabat in terra Austri: et egressus est Isaac exerceri in campo ad vesperam. Terra Austri, Geraram signat, unde a patre ad immolandum quondam fuerat adductus. Quod autem ait, Et egressus est, ut exerceretur in campo, quod Graece dicitur, ἀδολεσχῆσαι, in Hebraeo legitur: Et egressus est Isaac, ut loqueretur in agro, inclinante jam vespera. Significat autem secundum illud, quod Dominus solus orabat in monte, etiam Isaac, qui in typo Domini fuit, ad orationem, quasi virum justum domo egressum: et vel nona hora, vel ante solis occasum, spirituales Deo victimas obtulisse.
